decision_rubric.accept: Literal expected statement, supplied subject/host authority, lifecycle timing and fixed-topic query interpretation agree with the versioned contract within the stated narrow scope.
decision_rubric.reject: The expected output contradicts the explicit supplied evidence or authority/partition contract.
decision_rubric.needs_revision: The supplied fixture cannot support a determinate structural expectation without clarifying its inputs or label.
decision_rubric.note: Harness gaps and qualification limits are separately recorded; acceptance is not a claim that all runtime checks or production quality gates pass.

R01.rule: The trusted host asserts subject and source role within an already authorized partition; a subject is not an access grant and a model cannot confer confirmation authority.

R02.rule: Mutation subject equals source subject; every non-establish lifecycle edit requires structured_confirmation.

R03.section: Admission and source identity; One Record/Revision lifecycle
R03.rule: A quote begins pending. A distinct host confirmation of the exact pending text and target revision makes it confirmed while retaining evidence. Change explicitly replaces a confirmed head at the supplied onset.

R04.rule: Conditions are exact host-context equalities and time ranges are half-open. Nil AsOf means current selection. Host-supplied onsets are not inferred from prose or ingestion arrival.

R05.rule: Current reads use confirmed applicable facts. Controlled aliases select one of four fixed topic keys; no arbitrary paraphrase, extraction or final-answer quality promise follows.

R06.rule: Each candidate uses a fresh store, authorized scope a (space-bot-a, workspace:alpha) and a fixed 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z clock.

R07.rule: Stable case ID is cand-<template-id>-<subject-index>; establish/confirm/change use source fragments f1/f2/f3, distinct effect keys, and returned exact target revisions. The reviewed follow-up runner reads before confirmation and validates returned current/alias identity and source mapping against the admitted effects.

common_reasoning.subject: The opaque subject is copied exactly into Source, Mutation and ReadRequest. Attribution rests on the explicit trusted-host input, not parsing I/我; neither this identity nor its text widens authorization.
common_reasoning.confirmation: f1 is user_quote and therefore pending; f2 has a distinct source fragment, structured_confirmation role, identical text and exact returned target revision. The proposed adoption is justified by the supplied host role only, not by the AI reviewer or model text.
common_reasoning.validity: The establish onset is the explicit host value 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Confirmation retains it. No expiry or exact conditions are supplied. At the fixed September clock the final verified statement is applicable; this does not establish temporal boundary coverage.
common_reasoning.aliases: Every supplied alias belongs to the fixed dictionary for the case key. Its expected hit is the full current statement in the first eight facts. This is controlled topic retrieval over one eligible lineage, not an arbitrary paraphrase or answer-quality judgment.

findings.finding: 208 case IDs reuse only 26 statement templates over 8 opaque subjects. The subject expansion supplies identity variants, not 208 independent semantic trajectories or statistically independent observations.

The reviewer is an independent AI subagent in the same Codex task, authorized by the user to substitute for manual review. human_reviewed_cases remains 0. This is not blind human annotation, a second provider judgment, or a production holdout.

Every candidate runs in its own store and contains one fact lineage. This set does not test same-store subject isolation, Space/LabelSet rejection, competing ranking, or real Recall@8 capacity under distractors.

An old-value alias such as tea, 茶, 中文, vegetarian or 素食 may retrieve a newer or negated current statement because it selects a fixed topic key. Acceptance does not call the old and new values synonyms or license a final answer to affirm the old preference.

All onsets (2026-01-01 and optional 2026-02-01) are explicit host fixture inputs, and all final reads occur at 2026-09-01. No candidate tests expiry, nil onset, historical boundary reads, exceptions, correction, denial, forgetting or context specificity.

The harness supplies structured mutations and confirmation roles directly, so it measures no extraction or confirmation UX correctness. Aliases are selected from the implementation's frozen dictionary. Independent label review does not remove that selection bias or qualify production model, natural paraphrase, background or final-answer quality.

Qualifiers such as morning, 尽量 and scheduling remain in literal text. Unconditioned metadata does not establish machine-readable time-of-day/context restrictions, nor may a consumer discard those qualifiers or infer residence.

template_decisions.reviewer_expected_current: I prefer coffee in the morning.
template_decisions.rationale: The speaker explicitly prefers morning coffee. Preserve the morning qualifier in the text; the unconditioned host metadata does not prove a morning-only context filter.

The later verified statement replaces tea with coffee as the drink preference. A tea query requests the controlled drink topic; it must return the current coffee statement, never assert that tea remains preferred.
The Chinese statement explicitly says the speaker prefers coffee. 咖啡 names the beverage and 饮品 names its topic; neither needs an inferred preference value.
The later Chinese statement explicitly changes the preference from tea to coffee. 茶 is accepted only as a drink-topic selector, not a synonym for the new coffee preference.

template_decisions.reviewer_expected_current: My morning drink is 咖啡。
template_decisions.rationale: The mixed-language statement identifies the speaker's morning drink as coffee. Preserve the morning qualifier and do not turn it into an all-day preference or a machine-interpreted condition.

template_decisions.reviewer_expected_current: My preferred beverage is still water.
template_decisions.rationale: The explicit verified change moves the preference from sparkling water to still water. Here still water is a beverage value, not a claim that the old sparkling preference continues.
The speaker explicitly selects oolong tea as an everyday drink. 饮料 and 饮品 are topic terms; 茶 is a category match. The exact oolong qualifier remains in the fact.
The statement explicitly attributes a vegetarian diet to the speaker. diet and vegetarian are appropriate controlled topic lookups; no stricter vegan restriction is inferred.
The Chinese first-person statement explicitly reports vegetarian eating. Preserve the exact wording; 素食 must not be upgraded to a more specific vegan or medical restriction.

The verified later statement explicitly negates the earlier vegetarian habit. The expected current text retains 不再; matching 素食 retrieves this negated current statement and does not affirm vegetarianism.
The verified later statement ends the vegetarian diet. The expected current text retains stopped; a vegetarian topic hit does not mean the user currently follows that diet.
The mixed-language first-person statement explicitly attributes vegetarian eating. Keep the full statement unchanged; the English and Chinese queries select the same diet topic.
The statement describes an attempt to eat lightly. Preserve 尽量 so a tentative practice is not converted into an absolute restriction; diet and 饮食 name the subject matter.
The speaker explicitly requests English replies. The language key and both query terms match that request; no language proficiency or nationality is inferred.
The speaker explicitly requests Chinese replies. Preserve this reply preference; 中文 and 语言 are topic lookups, not evidence of nationality or other identity.
The verified later request changes replies from Chinese to English. 中文 can select the controlled language topic, but the returned current text must remain the English request.
The verified later statement changes the reply preference from English to Chinese. The expected current text directly states the new Chinese reply preference.
The mixed-language statement explicitly names Chinese as the preferred language. Keep its general wording instead of inventing proficiency or a more specific use context.
The Chinese statement explicitly requests Chinese as the reply language. Both aliases select the language topic without altering the request.
The request explicitly sets English as the reply language. The trusted subject attributes this request; no textual named-entity inference is needed.
The first-person statement explicitly supplies Asia/Shanghai as its timezone. Preserve the zone identifier and do not infer physical residence or a fixed UTC offset.
The Chinese first-person statement explicitly supplies Asia/Shanghai. 时区 and time zone identify the timezone topic; the IANA-style identifier stays unchanged.
The verified later statement explicitly changes the timezone from UTC to Asia/Tokyo. The expected current fact contains Tokyo; no old UTC preference should be adopted now.

The statement sets a scheduling timezone, not necessarily the speaker's residence. Accept the host-assigned subject and preserve the scheduling wording; do not broaden it into a physical-location fact.

template_decisions.reviewer_expected_current: 我的时区现在改为 Asia/Tokyo。
template_decisions.rationale: The verified Chinese statement explicitly changes the timezone from UTC to Asia/Tokyo. The exact new zone and change wording remain in the current fact.

The statement sets the timezone used for scheduling. The trusted subject supplies attribution; preserve the scheduling scope and do not infer residence or a constant offset across daylight-saving changes.
